glosses: aversion, disgust, repugnance

examples.text: Он отстрани́л её рука́ми и отошёл, и ей показа́лось, что лицо́ его́ выража́ло отвраще́ние и доса́ду.
examples.translation: He repulsed her with both hands; and his face seemed to express repugnance and vexation.
examples.english: He repulsed her with both hands; and his face seemed to express repugnance and vexation.

examples.text:

glosses: устар. действие по значению гл. отвращать, отвратить

examples.text: Он думал, что клятва церковная достаточна для отвращения людей слабых от подобных заблуждений.

glosses: устар. предотвращение, устранение чего-либо

examples.text: Попечительное начальство приняло все меры для отвращения голода и монополий перекупщиков.

glosses: крайняя неприязнь, в высшей степени отрицательное чувство по отношению к кому-либо или чему-либо

examples.text: И с отвращением читая жизнь мою, // Я трепещу и проклинаю, // И горько жалуюсь, и горько слёзы лью, // Но строк печальных не смываю.
И почувствовал к ней отвращение и дал себе слово стать другим человеком.

translations.source_sense_description: действие по значению гл. отвращать, отвратить

glosses: Opposition or repugnance of mind; fixed dislike often without any conscious reasoning.

examples.text: Due to her aversion to the outdoors she complained throughout the entire camping trip.
Live with aversion to classic men's wear, likely die with aversion to classic men's wear.
The other patients in the ward, all but the Texan, shrank from him with a tenderhearted aversion from the moment they set eyes on him the morning after the night he had been sneaked in.

glosses: An object of dislike or repugnance.

examples.text: Pushy salespeople are a major aversion of mine.

glosses: The act of turning away from an object.

translations.source_sense_description: действие по значению гл. отвращать, отвратить

glosses: To cause an intense dislike for something.

examples.text: It disgusts me to see her chew with her mouth open.

Tuc[ca]. […] Can thy Author doe it impudently enough? / Hiſt[rio]. O, I warrant you, Captaine: and ſpitefully inough too; he ha's one of the moſt ouerflowing villanous wits, in Rome. He will ſlander any man that breathes; If he diſguſt him. / Tucca. I'le know the poor, egregious, nitty Raſcall; and he haue ſuch commendable Qualities, I'le cheriſh him: […]

Mud This is a very specious piece of business; and above my implication—Dear me—dear me—what a thing it is, that one never can disgust one’s meals in peace—but one must be torn piecemeal with defamations—convocations—and other informalities—If I’d any of the fees and requisites of office for my pains—it would be a different thing—but every body knows I’m an ignoramous, and commit justice gratis—I must disperse the complaint.

1874, Marcus Clarke, For the Term of His Natural Life Chapter V
It is impossible to convey, in words, any idea of the hideous phantasmagoria of shifting limbs and faces which moved through the evil-smelling twilight of this terrible prison-house. Callot might have drawn it, Dante might have suggested it, but a minute attempt to describe its horrors would but disgust.

glosses: An intense dislike or loathing someone feels for something bad or nasty.

examples.text: With an air of disgust, she stormed out of the room.

translations.source_sense_description: действие по значению гл. отвращать, отвратить

glosses: Extreme aversion, repulsion.

examples.text: She felt a deep repugnance toward violence.
He showed open repugnance at the suggestion.
moral repugnance
sense of repugnance
express repugnance

glosses: Contradiction, inconsistency, incompatibility, incongruity; an instance of such.

examples.text: Discourses vain, inconsistant, and full of repugnances and contradictions.
